### Summary

<!-- Begin your issue with a one sentence summary -->
Zeta constantly gives empty whitespace suggestions, whether it is adding or removing whitespace. It does this continuously.

### Description
<!--  Describe with sufficient detail to reproduce from a clean Zed install.
  - Any code must be sufficient to reproduce (include context!)
  - Include code as text, not just as a screenshot.
  - Issues with insufficient detail may be summarily closed.
-->

Examples (each code-block is a separate example):
```Go
result, err := e.Client.OrderSend(ctx, *requests)
// I enter a newline here, and it suggests to remove it right away (while still in insert mode).
if err != nil {
	return fmt.Errorf("failed to send order: %w", err)
}
```

```Go
result, err := e.Client.OrderSend(ctx, *requests)
if err != nil {
	// I enter a newline here, then go back to normal mode (vim) and delete it with 'dd', it then immediately gives a jump suggestion to add the empty line again
	return fmt.Errorf("failed to send order: %w", err)
}
```

**Expected Behavior**: No empty whitespace suggestions should appear, only suggestions that contain some amount of characters, whether code or comments.

**Actual Behavior**: Zeta often gives suggestions that are completely empty, only adjusting whitespace. This should be handled by the user or formatter instead, not by AI.

body:
### Summary

Tab shouldn't accept edit predictions when the indentation is incorrect, but it still does most of the time.

### Description

https://zed.dev/docs/ai/edit-prediction#edit-predictions-conflict says that the Tab key shouldn't accept edit predictions "when your cursor isn't at the right indentation level".

```python
class Mixin(AsyncContextManagerMixin):
    @override
    @asynccontextmanager
    async def __asynccontextmanager__(self) -> AsyncGenerator[Self]:
        async with self.httpx, self.datadome:
            if not hasattr(self, "credentials"):
                self.credentials = await self.login(self.email)

            self.email = "xxx@gmail.com"
            self.user_id = xxx
            logger.debug("Email<normal>: {}</normal>", self.email)

            yield self
```

Steps to trigger the problem:
1. Copy the code snippet into a Python buffer
2. Insert some newlines above `self.email = ...`
3. Press Tab to indent to either 12 or 16 spaces, like you wanted to add some code

**Expected Behavior**: Tab should never accept edit predictions until the indentation reaches at least 12 spaces (at least I think this is what the docs mean)
**Actual Behavior**: Tab will trigger an edit predictions most of the time

<details><summary>Screen recording</summary>

* At 3 seconds, my cursor is not indented at all, and the edit prediction deletes the line
* At 7 seconds, pressing Tab once creates the correct indentation because of the LSP (I think?), not an edit prediction
* At 15s, the indentation level is too low, but the edit prediction still deletes the line

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/587c8e74-71e3-48e9-a63f-ba97a76a9a1a

</details>

### Summary

<!-- Begin your issue with a one sentence summary -->
Zed is ignoring the project settings edit prediction provider value.

### Description
<!--  Describe with sufficient detail to reproduce from a clean Zed install.
  - In your global zed settings JSON set `feature.edit_prediction.provider: "copilot"`
  - In your project settings change set `feature.edit_prediction.provider: "zed"`

-->

When you set the edit predictions provider in your project settings to a different value than that in the global settings, Zed it will ignore it. 

This behaviour seems unwanted, as you might want to use zeta for personal or OSS work and co-pilot for work related projects. Edit prediction settings do work correctly, respecting the values inside the project settings.

Steps to reproduce:
1. In your global zed settings JSON set `feature.edit_prediction.provider: "copilot"`
2. In your project settings change set `feature.edit_prediction.provider: "zed"`

**Expected Behavior**:
For this project it will use Zeta instead of copilot
**Actual Behavior**:
Still uses copilot

### Summary

Partial accept accepts the whole block in some situations. In that same context, when also in vim mode, the cursor jumps to the end of the suggestion.

I'm not exactly sure what situations this happens in but it seems to be either at the end of a line or end of a syntactic scope.

### Description

I've included a couple videos to hopefully capture the behavior.

Case 1:
- Vim mode disabled
- put the cursor at the end of a keymap dict and type ','
- zetta suggests a completion. I want to partially accept it

Actual Behavior:
cmd-ctrl-right accepts the entire selection

Expected Behavior:
cmd-ctrl-right should move to the next line and partially accept leading whitespace, then word by word.


Case 2:
- Vim mode enabled, normal mode
- enter insert mode  (eg shift-A)
- the cursor visually moves to the end of the completion but if I type, it inserts at the expected location.

- If I first arrow-up, the same bug exists where I can't partially accept with cmd-ctrl-right.

### Summary

Recently ZED_PREDICT_EDITS_URL was removed. The removal makes it very difficult to use a custom edit prediction backend.

### Description
A few hours ago in #30290 the feature to use ZED_PREDICT_EDITS_URL was removed. It now becomes unnecessary complicated to set a custom URL. Implementing a backend handling the EditPredict api has already been made by the community, see for instance https://github.com/praktiskt/zedex/blob/cdeda38fb5a93e64e43c1587d27b782c59cd6ca7/src/zed/edit_predict.go#L28 -- but now one must forego zed logon to use it.

Previously I could just use any custom edit predict backend, including Zeta-based backend.

<!-- Please insert a one line summary of the issue below -->
If I open Zed and it has file I have to close and reopen them to make Edit Predictions work

### Description
<!--  Describe with sufficient detail to reproduce from a clean Zed install. -->
When I launch Zed (0.181.5) on my Arch Linux and Zed has files already opened the Edit Predictions don't work, at the bottom in the Edit Predictions Icon there is a grey circle at its bottom:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e42af47f-dadb-45d7-b92a-603c38b147e4)

If I hover it there is a "Hidden For This File" message. There is also a "Edit Prediction Ctrl-Shift-I" a shortcut that when pressed has no effect:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ac06472d-6659-47b9-b0f9-c443178ca85f)

Clicking the icon shows a menu, if I try to click on "This Buffer" the menu closes and nothing happens:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c8814f9c-8130-4da6-a336-a123599a4c7a)

The _Toolbar \ Quick Actions \ Editor Controls_ Menu does not show Edit Predictions.

But if I close and reopen the file it all starts working again for the file I reopened, also if I open a file that was not open it works for this file as well.

Edit: Just found out if I have a window/instance of Zed where the Edit Predictions are working fine and launch another project instance the Edit Predictions on the new instance will also work just fine even with the files already opened.

Edit, **Workaround**: For now I created a dummy project/workspace that has not files opened, before I launch my real projects I launch the dummy one to get Edit Predictions to kick in, I then open a real project and close the dummy one. Better than having to closing all files, reopening them and re-splitting the editor panes the way I need.

Actual Behavior: Edit Predictions don't work for files already opened when I launch Zed.
Expected Behavior: Edit predictions should work without the need to close and reopen files.


### Zed Version and System Specs

Zed: v0.181.5 (Zed) 
OS: Linux X11 cachyos unknown
Memory: 62.6 GiB
Architecture: x86_64
GPU: AMD Radeon RX 7600 (RADV NAVI33) || radv || Mesa 25.0.3-cachyos1.2

Even if I clear my settings.json the problem persists.

### Summary

When enabling `features.edit_prediction_provider: "copilot"`, no edit predictions appear. Neither automatically (because `edit_predictions.mode: "eager"` is configured, nor on-demand by running the `editor: show edit prediction` or `copilot: suggest` actions.

<!-- Include all steps necessary to reproduce from a clean Zed installation. Be verbose -->
Steps to trigger the problem:
1. Configure GitHub Copilot as the edit predictor.
2. (Optional, not related) Confirm that it does work in the Assistant panel
3. Write some code and see no suggestions

When switching to the `zed` provider, it immediately shows results.

Actual Behavior:
No suggestions being shown.

Expected Behavior:
Suggestions being shown.

1. Have a bunch of text in your buffer
2. Select a couple of lines (x)
3. Delete them (d)
4. They'll be deleted. Cool.
5. Repeat steps 2-3. The selected lines won't be deleted.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aa29bcfa-6d06-4695-b64b-c47df21d370d
